title: Kigali Data Collection: May - Aug 2025
paragraphs: PhD student Eliane Nirere, was part of a field team collecting data for the Energy Transition Demand Modeling Study for Rwanda.

Surveys in Uganda and Kenya show that even low-income households are already incorporating electricity into their daily routines, especially for boiling water, as part of a "fuel stacking" strategy. Although their absolute electricity consumption may be low, small increases—from 5 to 7 kWh or from 10 to 14 kWh per month—could represent significant relative growth, up to 40%. Introducing low-cost electric kettles could provide these households with convenience and a pathway to modern, clean cooking solutions. For those consuming electricity within the lifeline tariff band of 0-15 kWh per month, electric cooking holds particular appeal. The objective of this project is to explore how targeted demand stimulation through an e-boiling program can create sustained electricity demand among low-income rural households that rely on biomass use.

Surveys were conducted with over 2,000 low income households in Kigali to gather information on household energy use and socio-economic and demographic information. Energy-efficient electric kettles were distributed to about 370 participating households through a cost-sharing scheme. Electricity consumption and appliance usage will be monitored over six months.

title: IDEAS Lab at the 2025 UW ECE Research Showcase (March 2025)
paragraphs: The IDEAS Research Lab was well represented at the 2025 UW ECE Research Showcase, where graduate researchers Ahana Mukherjee , Eliane Nirere , and Kwame Donkor presented posters on their cutting-edge work advancing sustainable and inclusive energy systems.

Ahana Mukherjee received the Best ECE Research Award for her poster on Distributed and Equitable Charging for Electric Three-Wheelers , which explores inclusive mobility solutions for underserved communities. View Poster »
Eliane Nirere presented her research on Electricity Demand Estimation for Mini-Grids , focusing on innovative approaches to improve energy planning in off-grid communities. View Poster »
Kwame Donkor shared his work on The Climate-Energy Nexus , investigating data-driven strategies to support resilient, low-carbon energy systems. View Poster »
Congratulations to all three for showcasing research that blends technical innovation with real-world impact. Learn more about the event here .

title: Third US-Africa Frontiers of Science, Engineering, and Medicine Symposium (Feb 2025)
paragraphs: PI Lukuyu participated in the Third U.S.-Africa Frontiers of Science, Engineering, and Medicine Symposium , held from February 18–20, 2025, in Kigali, Rwanda. Hosted by the U.S. National Academies in partnership with the Republic of Rwanda, the symposium brought together early- and mid-career researchers from across the U.S. and Africa to explore interdisciplinary solutions to global challenges. The event featured sessions on decarbonization, precision agriculture, biotechnology, space research, and smart cities, with opportunities for collaboration and knowledge exchange across borders and disciplines.

Dr. Lukuyu presented a poster titled “Driving Decarbonization: Centering Communities in Africa’s Transition to Electric Public Transportation” , highlighting her work on equitable and community-led approaches to sustainable mobility in African cities.

title: Kigali Data Collection: August 2024
paragraphs: Miquilina Anagbah led data collection for the project: Multi-Stakeholder Perspectives of Electric Bus Service in Kigali, Rwanda. in collaboration with students from the University of Rwanda, College of Science and Technology. We conducted surveys with about 800 electric and diesel bus passengers across Kigali to collect information on bus service satisfaction and perception of electric buses. This project is supported by BasiGO and USAID.

title: Summer 2024 Undergraduate Research Experience
paragraphs: We had the pleasure of welcoming Biniyam Gebreyohannes, a fellow from the UW Clean Energy Bridge to Research Program (CEBR), and Lillian Nguyen, a Clean Energy Institute ALVA fellow, for their Summer Research Experience. Biniyam explored how weather patterns affect Minigrid electricity behavior, drawing insights from the Katiirwe solar Minigrid in Western Uganda. Meanwhile, Lillian investigated Climate and Energy Injustice, focusing on racial and income disparities in access to indoor comfort. They were mentored by Ahana, Kwame, and Miquilina.

title: New York City Climate Week: September 2024
paragraphs: June Lukuyu attended several events during NYC Climate Week , including Climate Change AI and Google DeepMind’s event, AI for Climate Action: From Data to Impact . At this event, she delivered a lightning talk titled " Enabling Smart Grids for Climate Resilience & Adaptation in Africa " to showcase their CCAI-sponsored project, alongside a panel discussion featuring collaborator Genevieve Flasplohler.

title: eGUIDE Annual Retreat in Rochester NY: September 12-14, 2024
paragraphs: We had the pleasure of participating in the annual eGUIDE retreat at the Rochester Institute of Technology, which provided a fantastic opportunity to connect with both new and returning eGUIDE members. The retreat commenced with an enlightening visit to the Niagara Power Vista, where attendees gained valuable insights into hydropower energy generation, followed by a visit to the breathtaking Niagara Falls State Park. During the retreat, Ahana and Kwame showcased their ongoing research through poster presentations, fostering engaging discussions among participants.

The eGUIDE initiative is a collaborative effort involving six esteemed institutions: the University of Massachusetts - Amherst, Carnegie Mellon University, Columbia University, Rochester Institute of Technology, University of Washington, and the Kigali Collaborative Research Centre . This partnership aims to transform the approaches used for planning and operations of electricity infrastructure in developing regions.
